[32040 Industry Project | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject equips you to manage with strategic analysis and design issues for corporate information systems environment, utilising a major case study to apply and reinforce prior knowledge. You'll learn to evaluate different system strategies and enhance your senior management and communication abilities. Learning is interactive, emphasising practical judgement and teamwork while working in an industry-like environment.

[32040 Industry Project | Learning and teaching activities]
This is a capstone subject that is comprised of tutorials and group meetings.

 Initial classes articulate subject organisation, requirements and direction. These are followed by weekly teamwork tutorials/meetings. Each week these provide students with verbal feedback from their tutors, so as to gauge their progress and gain ideas for future direction.

 Students access Canvas to view videos, reference materials and communication tools. By accessing Canvas, students are informed in a wide range of material, from how to form their groups to how to prepare and develop their assessment tasks.

 Being a capstone project, this online learning is then used as reference materials for use with tutorial and group meetings, where students are required to work collaboratively as a project team. They are guided and encouraged to have their own team meetings and thereby further develop the project. Students are encouraged to use collaborative technologies outside face-to-face meetings.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32040 Industry Project | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Identify the requirements for an industry based information system in a medium to large and complex organisation. (B.1)
SLO2: Design an appropriate information systems solution, assess its impact on the organisation and make management recommendations. (C.1)
SLO3: Design and implement a strategy for introducing change to a complex corporate information system. (C.1)
SLO4: Engage in decision making in areas of uncertainty in a complex project. (D.1)
SLO5: Clearly communicate contributions of practical situations and changes to a range of audiences. (E.1)
